answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed dune-restoration plot where the holder replants native grasses under a ranger's watch, the plot's boundary marked by an opal-inlaid survey stone and its night sky logged against a catalogued nebula. Random spot-checks summon the holder to their own dune within a day, and one worker cannot tend two plots at once. The restoration fee in outside money doubles per further plot on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another real plot, another season of dune labor, another human, and twice the prior fee.
